verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents some event-driven automation. There is an 'Adaptive triggers' capability, guarded rollouts that progressively increase traffic while monitoring selected metrics for regressions, and webhooks that send an HTTP POST when a flag changes. However, the evidence only titles adaptive triggers without describing how they work, and it never shows a general user-defined 'when event X, do action Y' rule engine. Targeting rules and scheduled changes are condition-based and time-based, not event-triggered. Missing for 10: documented detail on trigger definitions and supported event sources, explicit automatic actions such as rollback on regression, a general-purpose automation rule builder, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
